messages.subject: Use same hyperparameters
parts:
Dear INLA group,

I am developing a model with a time-constant spatial effect and a time-varying spatial effect:

f(s0, model=spde) + 
f(s1, model=spde, group=s1.group, control.group=list(model="ar1", hyper=rho_cp, scale.model=TRUE))

Is it possible to set same hyperparamter kappa on these two spde models?

Thanks,
Ruby

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Use same hyperparameters
parts:
yes, but you need to make 's0' a replicate of 's1'. maybe also use copy if
you're keen on using the sum.

f(s1, ..., group=g, replicate=r1, nrep=2) +
f(s2, copy="s1", group=g2, replicate=r2)


where r1 are all 1's and r2 are all 2's, and g2 are all 1's.

for 's2' you'll get more than you need, as you only want the for for index in
group and the 2'nd replicate

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Use same hyperparameters
parts:
here is a small example (without the group, but that is easy to add)


m <- 98
n <- 100
phi <- 0.99
x0 <- scale(arima.sim(n, model = list(ar = phi)))
eta <- c()
xx <- list()
for(i in 1:m) {
xx[[i]] <- scale(arima.sim(n, model = list(ar = phi)))
eta <- c(eta, x0 + xx[[i]])
}

s <- 0.01
y <- eta + rnorm(n*m, sd = s)

## we let x0 be replicate m+1

res <- inla(y ~ -1 +
f(idx1, model = "ar1", nrep = m + 1, replicate = r1) +
f(idx2, copy = "idx1", replicate = r2, nrep = m+1),
data = data.frame(y,
idx1 = rep(1:n, m),
idx2 = rep(1:n, m),
r1 = rep(1:m, each = n),
r2 = rep(m+1, n*m)
),
family = "normal",
control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1/s^2),
fixed = TRUE))))


par(mfrow = rep(ceiling(sqrt(m)), 2))
plot(res$summary.random$idx2$mean[m*n + 1:n], x0); abline(a=0,b=1)
for(i in 1:m) {
plot(res$summary.random$idx1$mean[(i-1)*n + 1:n], xx[[i]])
abline(a=0,b=1)
}
plot(eta, res$summary.linear.predictor$mean)
abline(a = 0, b = 1)
